focus.jtag: U.S. destroyed five Iranian tankers overnight; Brent crosses $100 for the first time since July, yields near 3-yr highs into a big data week
focus.jnote: The tape stays under an oil-and-war cloud. Overnight the U.S. military destroyed five Iranian crude tankers in retaliation for an attempted attack on an American warship, and Brent crude crossed $100 for the first time since July (last ~$100.4, +2.6%), with WTI for November near $95. Goldman Sachs said intensifying shipping attacks are raising the probability of Brent exceeding $120 a barrel. Equity futures are mixed — tech futures edging slightly higher into Apple’s product event, benchmark futures roughly flat — but the oil bid keeps the 10-year yield near three-year highs (~4.79%), and markets price ~60% odds of a September rate hike. PPI hits Thursday and CPI Friday, with the FOMC 9/15–16. A live, open-ended conflict stacked on a CPI/FOMC week is not a premium-selling setup.
focus.notdown: Energy (XLE, XOM, MPC, OXY) and Defense (LMT, RTX, NOC) keep the fundamental bid — oil supply fear lifts energy, conflict-demand lifts defense. But these are two-sided war trades, not clean Snipers: any credible Hormuz-reopening or ceasefire headline gaps energy straight back down (recall the March episode when Brent fell ~9% in a session on de-escalation signals). Watch-only, and note the scanner boarded none of them today.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive growth and fuel-sensitive transports (airlines) are the pressured groups — higher oil and a ~4.79% 10-year weigh on both. But selling bear calls into a VIX ticking up off its lows, with PPI in a day, CPI in two, and an FOMC next week that can reprice the curve either way, is exactly the blow-up 4-VAL exists to prevent. The disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite 61 is squarely WARM and P(≥1% gap) at 41% is above the 35% trigger — either one alone locks out GREEN. Layer on a live U.S.–Iran military exchange with Brent above $100, plus PPI (Thu 9/10), CPI (Fri 9/11) and the FOMC (9/15–16) all inside a normal DTE, and the overnight tail is skewed and hard to size. The full-universe scanner boarded zero names. Stand down on new credit spreads, or if you must be positioned, use 7-DTE that clears CPI and the FOMC and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

risks: Iran retaliation & Strait of Hormuz — the U.S. destroyed five Iranian tankers overnight and Aramco facilities were reportedly hit; roughly a fifth of the world’s oil moves through Hormuz. Any escalation or closure sends crude vertical — Goldman already flags Brent-above-$120 risk. The week’s biggest tail.

August CPI · Fri 9/11 (PPI · Thu 9/10) — the cleaner Fed signal before the FOMC, and with Brent above $100 feeding inflation fear an upside surprise is more likely than usual. Headline CPI is seen ~3.4%; a hot print stacked on the oil shock is the worst-case macro combination.
FOMC · Mon–Wed 9/15–16 — a live hike-or-hold meeting; markets price ~60% odds of a 25bp hike after August payrolls (+162K). Any spread must expire before this.

Oil & the 10-year — Brent ~$100 / WTI ~$95 keeps inflation fear alive; the 10Y is near a three-year high (~4.79%, briefly above 4.8%). A renewed oil pop compounds pressure on stocks and hardens the hike case.

Apple event today; single-stock landmines — Apple’s annual product launch can swing megacap tech, and pharma remains headline-sensitive (Amgen fell ~10% Tuesday). Keep every spread clear of its name’s catalyst.
